clues.text: When Moses stretched his staff toward heaven, the LORD sent thunder and this upon Egypt, with lightning flashing.
It struck all of Egypt during the plagues, but never fell in Goshen, where the Israelites lived.
As the Amorites fled from Joshua's army near Beth-horon, the LORD threw it down, and it killed more than Israel's swords did.
Pharaoh's officials who feared the LORD's word rushed their servants and livestock into shelter before it came.
In John's vision, pieces of it weighing almost a hundred pounds each fell, and men cursed God.
In Egypt it destroyed the ripe barley and blooming flax, but the later wheat and spelt were spared.
God asked Job whether he had seen its storehouses, held in reserve for the day of war and battle.
